```{r}
read_output <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path("..", "outputs", "tables", paste0(name, ".csv"))

figure_path <- function(name) file.path("..", "outputs", "figures", name)
```

# Executive Summary

This report is generated from pipeline outputs. It never embeds hand-copied model
estimates. The current risk table and the rolling comparison below exist only after a
successful run.

```{r}
knitr::kable(read_output("current_copula_risk"), digits = 5)
```

# Risk Question

How do conditional volatility, non-Gaussian marginal risk, and cross-asset dependence
affect one-step portfolio VaR and ES, and do the forecasts remain calibrated out of sample?

# Data and Portfolio Definition

```{r}
if (file.exists(figure_path("asset_prices.png"))) knitr::include_graphics(figure_path("asset_prices.png"))
```

# Currency and Return Conventions

Negative returns are losses. VaR and ES are positive loss magnitudes. Portfolio simple
return is the weighted sum of asset simple returns; exact portfolio log return is
`log1p(portfolio_simple_return)`. Local-index-return mode performs no FX conversion.
Base-currency mode instead requires aligned FX returns quoted as base-currency units per
unit of asset currency. VaR, ES, and realised rolling observations are reported and
compared in the configured `portfolio.return_type` space; all supplied profiles use log
returns.

# Exploratory Analysis

Price and return artefacts are generated from the validated aligned data, never from
manual report inputs.

# ARMA-GARCH Marginal Models

Candidate ARMA orders, volatility families, distributions, solvers, and diagnostics are
configuration driven. Every failed fit remains in the selection table.

# Model Selection

```{r}
selection <- read_output("marginal_model_selection")
knitr::kable(selection[selection$selected %in% TRUE | selection$convergence %in% FALSE, ], digits = 4)
```

# Residual Diagnostics

Selection first enforces convergence and parameter validity, then evaluates standardised
and squared-residual Ljung-Box tests.

# PIT Transformation

PIT values are clipped strictly inside `(0,1)` before inverse-CDF evaluation, and clipping
counts are retained in model diagnostics.

# Copula Dependence Modelling

```{r}
knitr::kable(read_output("copula_model_selection"), digits = 4)
if (file.exists(figure_path("copula_diagnostic.png"))) knitr::include_graphics(figure_path("copula_diagnostic.png"))
```

# Tail Dependence

Lower-tail dependence is the relevant coefficient for joint extreme negative returns on
the return-CDF scale. Upper-tail dependence describes joint extreme positive returns and
is not labelled crash dependence.

# Monte Carlo Simulation

Joint uniforms are transformed through the selected marginal inverse PITs, conditional
means and volatilities are restored, and asset log returns are converted to simple returns
before portfolio aggregation.

```{r}
if (file.exists(figure_path("simulation_risk.png"))) knitr::include_graphics(figure_path("simulation_risk.png"))
```

# Portfolio VaR

VaR is a loss-quantile threshold, not a maximum loss.

# Expected Shortfall

ES is the mean loss beyond the VaR threshold under the configured tail convention.

# Benchmark Comparison

`runtime_seconds` is elapsed wall-clock time. It can include host suspension; the full-run

should not be interpreted as CPU time.


# Monte Carlo Convergence

The full profile repeats configured simulation counts and seeds. A convergence result is
reported only when that optional stage has run.

# Sensitivity Analysis

Confidence levels, windows, weights, innovation distributions, and copula families are
controlled in YAML profiles and can be varied without code changes.

# Computational Performance

Stage timings and failed-fit counts are retained in logs and result tables. Simulations
are chunked; rolling forecasts are checkpointed and resumable. A fixed seed and fixed
chunk size are reproducible, but changing chunk size can remap the random stream to
bivariate draws and therefore change the exact Monte Carlo result.

# Limitations

The default cross-index demonstration uses local-index-return mode and therefore does not
claim a base-currency investable portfolio. Rotated and Archimedean copulas require the
optional dependence package. ES evaluation includes descriptive residuals and a joint
score but is not presented as a formal ES hypothesis test.

# Reproducibility

Use the profile runners in `scripts/`, or set `PRA_CONFIG` and execute the targets pipeline.
Seeds and actual simulation counts are stored with outputs.

# Conclusion

Conclusions must be drawn from the generated backtest table. No model is declared best
from a single p-value.
